newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Iraq seen staying out of Colombo tea auction.
newsitem.headline: Iraq seen staying out of Colombo tea auction.

text.p: Iraq, once the biggest buyer of Sri Lankan tea but forced from the market by a U.N. trade embargo, is unlikely to return to the Colombo auction soon, an official with the island's biggest tea exporter said on Tuesday.

"It is very unlikely Iraq will re-enter the Colombo tea auction in the near future because of financial problems and because our tea prices are too high," said an official at Akbar Brothers, once the biggest exporter of Ceylon tea to Iraq.
Akbar Brothers exported 23.8 million kg in 1996, making it the biggest exporter of Ceylon tea.
Iraq has been out of the Colombo tea auction for the last seven years because of the United Nations trade embargo imposed after the 1990 invasion of Kuwait, the official said.
But Baghdad has been allowed since December to import food under a United Nations-monitored oil-for-food arrangement.
The Akbar Bros official said Iraq can buy tea from Indonesia and Vietnam at half the price of Ceylon tea.
Tea prices at the Colombo auctions soared to record highs late last year because of strong winter demand from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
Tea Board officials said prices should remain firm this year but off last year's record highs.
Exporters said much of the tea imported by Turkey and Jordan is either smuggled or re-exported across their borders to Iraq.
"Traders in Turkey and Jordan buy the cheapest tea from Sri Lanka and smuggle it across to Iraq," the official said.

Ceylon tea exports to Turkey rose by 138 percent to 31 million kg in 1996, making it the second-biggest importer of Sri Lankan tea after the CIS. Much of the tea, however, is re-exported to the mainly Moslem southern CIS republics.
Jordan imported 15.6 milion kg of tea from Sri Lanka in 1996.
